User model, auth views, profile routing.

## Purpose

Owns the custom `User` model, the login/register/settings/logout flows, and the URL routing for `/profile/<username>` (the actual profile rendering logic lives in `apps/articles/views.py::profile_view` — this app just keeps the URLs and the delegating shims).

- `User.USERNAME_FIELD = "email"` — auth uses email, not the username field, for login. `username` is a display/URL handle only.

===profiles-and-following.feature===
Feature: Profiles and following
  As a member of the community
  I want to view other users' profiles and follow or unfollow them
  So that I can curate whose articles I care about

  Background:
    Given users have public profiles identified by their username
    And a profile shows the articles the user has authored or favorited

  Rule: A profile is addressed by username and only exists for a real user

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-PROFILE-001
    Scenario: Viewing an existing user's profile shows their authored articles
      Given a user who has authored an article
      When anyone views that user's profile
      Then the profile is shown
      And the user's authored articles appear on it

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-PROFILE-002
    Scenario: A profile's favorites view shows the articles that user has favorited
      Given a user who has favorited an article
      When anyone views the favorites tab of that user's profile
      Then the favorited articles appear

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-PROFILE-003
    Scenario: Viewing a profile for an unknown username is not found
      Given no user is registered with a given username
      When anyone tries to view a profile for that username
      Then the profile is reported as not found

  Rule: A profile view reflects the viewer's relationship to it

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-PROFILE-VIEWER-001
    Scenario: A user viewing their own profile is recognised as themselves
      Given a signed-in user
      When the user views their own profile
      Then the profile is marked as the viewer's own
      And the profile does not indicate that the viewer follows themselves

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-PROFILE-VIEWER-002
    Scenario: A profile indicates whether the viewer already follows it
      Given a signed-in user who follows another user
      When the follower views that other user's profile
      Then the profile indicates that the viewer is already following

  Rule: Following requires being signed in and is performed by explicit submission

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-FOLLOW-001
    Scenario: An anonymous visitor cannot follow
      Given the visitor is not signed in
      When the visitor submits a request to follow a user
      Then the visitor is redirected to the sign-in page

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-FOLLOW-002
    Scenario: Following a non-existent user is not found
      Given a signed-in user
      When the user submits a request to follow a username that does not exist
      Then the request is reported as not found

  Rule: Following toggles between following and not following the target user

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-FOLLOW-003
    Scenario: Following then following again unfollows
      Given a signed-in user who does not yet follow a target user
      When the user submits a follow request for that target
      Then the user is now following the target
      When the user submits a follow request for that same target again
      Then the user is no longer following the target

  Rule: The follow action responds in place for live interactions and otherwise redirects

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-FOLLOW-RESPONSE-001
    Scenario: A live follow toggle updates the follow control in place
      Given a signed-in user performing the follow action as a live page interaction
      When the user toggles following on a target user
      Then the follow control is returned for in-place update without a full page navigation

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-FOLLOW-RESPONSE-002
    Scenario: A plain follow submission redirects back to the profile
      Given a signed-in user performing the follow action as a plain submission
      When the user toggles following on a target user
      Then the user is redirected back to that user's profile
===domain/user.feature===
Feature: User identity and following relationships
  As the steward of the user model
  I want the identity and following rules to hold as invariants
  So that authentication and the social graph behave consistently everywhere

  Background:
    Given a user has an email address, a username display handle, an optional bio, and an optional profile image

  Rule: The email address is the identity credential and the username is a display handle

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-USER-IDENTITY-001
    Scenario: The email is the field used to identify a user for authentication
      Given a user account
      Then the user is identified for authentication by their email address
      And the username serves as a separate display and URL handle

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-USER-IDENTITY-002
    Scenario: A user's display names resolve to the username
      Given a user with a username
      Then both the user's full name and short name resolve to that username

  Rule: A user created without a password cannot authenticate with a password

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-USER-PASSWORD-001
    Scenario: Creating a user with a password yields a usable password
      When a user is created with a password
      Then that password can be verified for the user
      And the user has a usable password

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-USER-PASSWORD-002
    Scenario: Creating a user without a password yields an unusable password
      When a user is created without a password
      Then the user has an unusable password
      And no password can be used to authenticate that user until one is set

  Rule: Superusers must have the administrative flags set

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-SUPERUSER-001
    Scenario: Creating a superuser sets the administrative flags
      When a superuser is created
      Then the account is a staff member
      And the account is a superuser
      And the account is active

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-SUPERUSER-002
    Scenario Outline: Creating a superuser without a required flag is rejected
      When a superuser is created with <flag> turned off
      Then the creation is rejected

      Examples:
        | flag         |
        | staff status |
        | superuser status |

  Rule: Following is a directional relationship between users

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-FOLLOW-GRAPH-001
    Scenario: A user is not following another by default
      Given two distinct users
      Then neither user is following the other

    @RID-ACCOUNTS-FOLLOW-GRAPH-002
    Scenario: Adding a follower makes the relationship hold in one direction only
      Given two distinct users
      When the first user begins following the second
      Then the first user is following the second
      And the second user is not thereby following the first

  Rule: Following oneself is never recorded

    # @unverified-intent: a self-follow submission is silently accepted as a no-op rather
    # than rejected with an error; stakeholders may want to confirm whether silently
    # ignoring it is preferable to surfacing an explicit "cannot follow yourself" response.
    @RID-ACCOUNTS-FOLLOW-GRAPH-003
    Scenario: A user cannot follow themselves
      Given a signed-in user
      When the user submits a request to follow themselves
      Then the user is not recorded as following themselves
      And the request completes without error

# Behavioral specs (FFFlow L3)

These Gherkin feature files are the **behavioral contract** for the app — what
it does, in present tense, in domain language. They were extracted from the
existing code by FFFlow's `characterize` step, so they describe current
behavior (characterization), not aspirations.

## Layout

One directory per bounded context (matching the Django apps + shared helpers):

```
docs/specs/
  accounts/    authentication, profiles & following, user model
  articles/    feeds, authoring, article model, markdown
  comments/    commenting, comment model
  helpers/     pagination, integrity-error classification, htmx detection
```

Acceptance specs live at a context root; domain/property specs live under
`<context>/domain/`. `*-properties.feature` files hold universal invariants
(tagged `@property-based`) suited to property-based testing with Hypothesis.

## RIDs (requirement IDs)

Every scenario carries a unique `@RID-{CONTEXT}-{NAME}-{NNN}` tag. The CONTEXT
segment matches the first directory under `docs/specs/`. These are the anchor
points for traceability: spec → test → code.

131 scenarios, 131 RIDs.

## Gates (both blocking, part of `just check-all`)

- **`just spec-audit`** — `specdrive audit`: every RID is well-formed, unique,
  and its CONTEXT matches its directory.
- **`just spec-verify`** — full spec→test traceability. Runs both test suites,
  emits a JUnit report from each, injects each test's RID(s), merges the
  reports, and runs `specdrive verify` with `strictTraceability` on.
  **131/131 RIDs covered, 0 uncovered.**

## How a test declares the scenario it covers

`specdrive verify` reads RIDs from the JUnit report as
`<property name="rid" value="RID-...">` inside each `<testcase>`. The Django
runner doesn't emit per-test properties, so the mapping lives in
`docs/specs/rid_map.*.yaml` (`"<classname>::<test_method>": [RID-...]`) and
`scripts/inject_rids.py` writes the properties into the report. 15 tests are
deliberately unmapped (`@NOSPEC`) — seed/CLI commands and bare GET-render
smoke tests with no behavioral scenario.

## Two test suites

- **Django suite** (`apps/*/tests.py`, `helpers/tests.py`, `manage.py test`) —
  the 124 example/behavioral tests, including `hypothesis.extra.django`
  property tests for DB-backed invariants (slug stability, email-identity,
  self-follow).
- **Property suite** (`specs/property/`, pytest + `pytest-bdd-property`) — binds
  the DB-free `@property-based` pagination scenarios directly to the Gherkin
  feature file; Hypothesis generates 100+ inputs per scenario.
